summary.headline: Priced near the top of its 5-year range, with modest growth
summary.takeaway: Investors pay more than usual for each dollar of Coca-Cola's profit and sales. Its P/E is a bit below peers, but growth is modest, so it only partly explains the higher price.

positives.text: P/E (price compared with yearly profit) is 28.7, below the peer median of 32.
Profit per share (EPS) grew about 11.6% a year over 3 years, and 8.1% over the past year.

watch_outs.text: P/E of 28.7 is higher than 89% of the last 5 years, above its 5-year median of 26.3.
P/S (price compared with yearly sales) is 8.23, near its 5-year high and far above the peer median of 2.27.
PEG (P/E compared with growth) is 5.19, as analysts expect only 5.5% EPS growth next year. Revenue grew 7.4%, below peers' 11.2%.

what_to_watch_next: Wall Street analysts' price targets range from $88.00 to $112.00, with a mean of $99.64, versus today's $97.62.
summary.ask_yourself: How comfortable are you paying a higher-than-usual price for a company growing at a modest pace?
